shots.composition_notes: Locked-off wide-ish medium two-shot of the couple centered in the kitchen, both figures full-torso-up and vertically centered between the window above and floor below, giving generous headroom. Camera does not move at all through the whole scene despite three different title-card overlays (episode number top-left, 'ADULT LOVE' lower-third, dialogue caption) being swapped over it. Kitchen set is symmetrical-ish around the window behind them, with takeout containers and clutter framing left and right edges to fill negative space rather than being cropped out.

Slow push in from the same static medium framing into a tight close-up on the two faces, cropping out the lower bodies and most of the countertop clutter that was visible in scene 0. The push settles with both faces occupying the upper two-thirds of frame, woman on the left third, man on the right two-thirds, noses nearly touching at the vertical centerline. Window and city lights behind them go soft/out of focus as the lens tightens, isolating the characters' exaggerated eye-rolls from the background.

Hard cut to a full-black end-card with centered serif title text ('LOW BATTERY PEOPLE' / 'CREATED BY NIN.') and a small ribbon graphic reading 'NEW EPISODE DAILY' anchored below center. No camera or subject in frame at all; pure graphic slate.

framing_patterns_notes: The whole clip is built from a single static two-shot that only moves once: a slow punch-in during the punchline delivery (dialogue captions 'at/same/what' land right as the zoom tightens), taking the couple from a wide establishing framing down to a close-up on their reaction faces before cutting to the black outro card. Title/caption text is consistently stacked in the same zones across the video (episode tag top-left, episode title lower-third or centered, spoken-line captions bottom-center) rather than the camera repositioning to accommodate them.
